transcript:
User: Hi, I got a flyer. How does this whole thing work exactly?
Agent: Got it, so you saw our flyer and you’re curious how this all works.  

At a high level, it makes sure you don’t lose money from missed calls — when someone rings your business and you’re busy or closed, we still answer, talk to them, and book the appointment or take the message so you don’t lose that customer.  

Before I go deeper, what kind of business are you running?
User: I own a hardware store. Sometimes I miss calls when I close early or step out. How's it installed, though?
Agent: Nice, a hardware store’s a perfect example for this.  

You don’t install anything physical — we connect on the phone side: either we forward your unanswered calls to our system, or set your line so that if you don’t pick up in a few rings (or you’re closed), it rolls over to us, we answer, help the caller, and text/email you the details.  

When you close early or step out now, do those calls usually hit voicemail or just ring out?
User: They usually hit voicemail. So, is there a cost for setting this up, and does it work with my current line?
Agent: Yeah, that makes sense — voicemail’s where a lot of those hardware-store orders just die.  

Yes, it works with your current line; we just set up call-forwarding rules (no new phone number needed), and there’s a one-time setup plus a monthly fee that depends on call volume.  

To give you real numbers instead of a range, roughly how many calls a day do you think you’re getting right now?
User: I'm not quite sure about the exact volume. Can you give me a general idea of costs first?
Agent: Totally fair, a lot of owners don’t have an exact count.  

Ballpark: most small–mid shops land somewhere in the low hundreds per month — think roughly a few hundred bucks on the low side up to maybe around a thousand if you’re really busy, depending on how many calls we’re actually handling.  

Given your hardware store, are you more like a small neighborhood shop or a larger store with steady foot traffic all day?
User: We're more of a small neighborhood shop. Let me think about this and I'll call you back if I decide.
Agent: Yeah, I hear you — you don’t want to jump into anything without being sure.  

Before we wrap, can I at least show you, using your own numbers, roughly how much those voicemail calls might be costing you each month so you know whether it’s even worth calling back?
User: I appreciate that, but I think I need to mull it over first. Thanks for your help.
Agent: Got it, I respect that you want to mull it over — if those missed calls start to bug you, just give us a ring and we can walk through your numbers and options in a couple minutes. Thanks for taking the time to talk today, and have a great rest of your day!
